title: Source manifest
description: Schema for the committed list of documentation entry points to seed the corpus. This file contains source references only. Third-party page content MUST NOT be committed (FR-032, SC-015), and this schema makes that structural rather than a matter of discipline: there is no field in which page content could be recorded, and every object is closed. If content ever needs to be carried, it belongs in the vector store, which is not in version control.

manifest_version.description: Identity of this manifest. Recorded on the crawl job so a corpus can be traced to the manifest that seeded it.

notes.description: Editorial notes — why these entry points, what is deliberately excluded, and any path whose crawling permission was checked.

name.description: Human-readable label shown in the source registry.

start_url.description: The entry point. Must be a public http or https address; the address guard refuses anything else before a connection is opened (FR-044). A path disallowed by the site's crawling directives is excluded here rather than worked around.

sitemap_url.description: The sitemap enumerating this source's documentation section, as declared in the host's own robots.txt. Measured 2026-10-01: the four support.atlassian.com sources expose 1-4 in-scope links each on their start_url, because the documentation navigation is rendered client-side and 656 of the 667 hrefs on access-a-project/ point at other products' directories. Link-following those four alone yields a corpus of REST API reference only, which cannot answer a single one of the curated questions about Jira user configuration, Confluence, or JSM. Declaring the sitemap is NOT an authorisation: every URL read from it passes the same robots gate as a link-derived one (FR-028), and is still held to this source's crawl scope. Null for a source that relies on link-following alone.

scope_prefix.description: Explicit crawl scope as an absolute path prefix, with a trailing slash. Derived from start_url when omitted, which is correct for an ARTICLE entry point (/docs/access-a-project/ scopes to /docs/) but too broad for a start_url that IS a section index: the derived rule drops the leaf segment, so /cloud/jira/platform/ would scope to /cloud/jira/ and silently pull in sibling sections such as /cloud/jira/software/. Any source whose start_url names a section rather than a page states its scope here.

product_domain.description: Product this source documents, e.g. 'jira', 'confluence'. Null for a cross-product entry point, which causes retrieval to span domains (FR-013).

allowed_domains.description: Hosts the crawl may reach from this entry point. Derived from start_url when omitted, and never permitted to widen beyond the registrant's entry point.

max_pages.description: Bounded crawl (FR-027), applied to this source alone. The six sources sum to a 155-page ceiling; SC-011 now states a 100-200 page corpus target, and a run over the six real sitemaps measured 154 pages queued.

max_depth.description: Traversal depth bound from the entry point (FR-027).

delay_seconds.description: Per-request delay between pages (FR-027). The crawler identifies itself honestly and respects the site's stated directives regardless of this value (FR-028).

notes.description: Why this source was chosen and what it is expected to cover.
